title: This Beetle Fires Boiling Spray in 500 Explosions a Second
subject: bombardier beetle

scenes.text: This tiny beetle fights back with explosions. Hundreds every second.
The bombardier beetle. Inside its tail, two chemicals wait in separate chambers.
When attacked, they mix. The reaction heats the spray to almost one hundred degrees Celsius.
It fires in pulses, up to about 500 a second. Each pulse is a tiny explosion.
The beetle swings its tail like a nozzle, and aims at whatever bit it.
A pulsing jet that hot would cook its own body, so the beetle gets to cool between bangs.

description:
A bombardier beetle shoots boiling chemical spray in hundreds of tiny explosions per second.
Two chemicals mix inside its abdomen, heat to near 100 degrees Celsius, and fire in rapid pulses that also give the chamber time to cool.
What other animal has the best built-in defence?
first_comment: Scientists say the pulsing is what stops the beetle from burning itself. Would you try to pick one up?
